A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MultiverSeg, and their main texts, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices support comparison. Internal inconsistencies in some dataset counts and result summaries can be identified and qualified using the corresponding tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated interactive-segmentation experiments, held-out segmentation results and context-quality analyses in Sections 6–7 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v2 reports original segmentation experiments and adds baseline comparisons, few-shot fine-tuning, resolution sensitivity, and measured inference time and memory usage.

M1.justification: The ScribblePrompt initialization, CrossBlock encoder-decoder, accumulating context set, segmentation loss and synthetic-task training procedure are retained. The added fine-tuning procedure is a comparator; the resolution changes concern evaluation rather than a revised MultiverSeg algorithm.

E1.justification: Table 2 adds TotalSegmentator: 1,204 CT scans covering 104 structures, substantially broadening organ, bone, muscle and vessel evaluation. The listed evaluation suite grows from 11 to 12 datasets. v1's appendix and dataset plots establish 59 sequential-evaluation tasks across seven datasets, versus 161 across eight in v2; v1 already contains an inconsistent 161-task statement in Section 6.1.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained ScribblePrompt, SP+UVS and UniverSeg comparisons, v2 actually evaluates SAM, MedSAM, SAM-Med2D, IMIS-Net and SegNext, and adds task-specific fine-tuned ScribblePrompt. Figures 3–4 and 18 report the expanded comparisons; MedSAM results appear in Section 6.2 and fine-tuning in Appendix E.4/Figure 21.

E3.justification: The principal sequential evaluation changes from 128x128 to 256x256, with model-specific input resizing and predictions rescaled before scoring; v2 also evaluates at 128x128. It adds a five-example fine-tuning protocol with a 4/1 training/validation split and 13 subsequent test images. In-context evaluations extend to 256 context examples, and interactive context-size evaluations extend from 32 to 64.

E4.justification: v2 adds resolution sensitivity analysis, inference-time and memory scaling, and a longer-sequence WBC analysis. These test sensitivity to evaluation resolution and practical scalability beyond v1's analyses. Existing context-label-quality and SP+UVS minimum-context analyses are retained as Figures 16–17, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The new fine-tuning experiment reports five random seeds and 95% confidence intervals; the runtime table reports mean and standard deviation over 1,000 predictions. Existing main experiments retain 200 simulations and the Experiment 2 description retains 100 bootstrap runs. These additions do not establish increased repetition of the existing experiments.

E6.justification: Reported click/scribble reductions change from 35.61%/52.70% to 36.41%/25.26%, with substantially revised result entries in v1 Table 7 versus v2 Figure 18. These reflect different resolution and dataset coverage, not same-setting performance changes. New comparator, fine-tuning, runtime and larger-context results expand the evidence substantially. The fine-tuning scribble mean is internally inconsistent, and Figure 21's scenario count disagrees with Appendix E.4.

T1.justification: The task objectives, CrossConv/CrossBlock mathematics, expected segmentation loss and equivalent implementation derivation are retained. v1's first two displayed equations become inline expressions and subsequent equations are renumbered; no substantive mathematical assumption, proof or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains interactive in-context segmentation without task-specific retraining. The quantitative headline is narrowed: abstract scribble savings change from 53% to 25%, and the conclusion replaces reductions of 'as much as 50%' in interactions with 36% average click savings.

C2.justification: v2 develops practical interpretations concerning fine-tuning overhead, interactive latency and resolution sensitivity. BUID heterogeneity was already discussed in v1's appendix; v2 refines that limitation with a small-context failure boundary and explains why informative scribbles reduce context's benefit. These are bounded extensions rather than a new account of the method's mechanism.

D1.justification: v2 adds square-padding and bilinear-resizing details, SAM's ViT-b/single-mask configuration, fine-tuning hyperparameters and checkpoint selection, and A100 timing/memory measurement details. The core architecture and training recipe were already documented. The new Code appendix repeats the existing code-and-weights link rather than establishing newly available resources.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to SAM-Med2D, the IMIS-Net benchmark paper, LesionLocator and interactive-latency research. These support expanded comparisons and practical discussion while preserving the central positioning relative to interactive segmentation, in-context learning and task-specific retraining.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most explanatory prose remain recognizable. v2 polishes wording, relocates the fine-tuning paragraph within Related Work, adds an appendix contents list and Code/Inference sections, and reorganizes supplementary experiment subsections. The added scientific material does not amount to wholesale narrative rewriting.

P2.justification: Figure 4 changes from differences in total interactions to grouped per-image comparisons, and v1's combined dataset plots become separate click and scribble figures. v2 expands qualitative and quantitative panels and adds fine-tuning, resolution and runtime displays. v1 Table 7 becomes the expanded tabular Figure 18; the architecture and segmentation-workflow illustrations are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central efficiency claim through broader evaluated baselines, whole-body CT coverage, higher-resolution evaluation, and explicit adaptation and resource-cost studies. These address important limitations in v1's comparison breadth and practical feasibility evidence. Reporting errors weaken some additions: Appendix E.4 repeats the click value for scribbles, and Figure 21 states 13/14 scenarios versus 13/16 in the text. Those defects require correction, but do not outweigh the substantial gains supported by the expanded experiments and figures.
